*   **Construction:** $O(P \cdot N^3)$ in the naive implementation (checking all primitives for all cells), but optimized to $O(P \cdot k)$ where $k$ is the average number of cells a primitive intersects, by only iterating over candidate cells defined by the primitive's AABB [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes two implementations of grid construction. The 'naive' implementation (first code snippet) iterates over all cells and, for each cell, checks all primitives, resulting in a complexity proportional to the total number of cells times the number of primitives ($O(Cells) * O(P)$, which is effectively $O(P)$ per cell or $O(P * N^3)$ if $N$ is GRIDSIZE). The 'final' or optimized implementation (second code snippet) iterates over primitives and, for each primitive, calculates its bounding box (AABB) to determine the specific range of cells it intersects, adding it only to those candidate cells. This reduces the complexity to being proportional to the number of primitives times the average number of cells they intersect ($k$), i.e., $O(P * k)$. The claim accurately reflects this transition and the associated complexity analysis provided in the text.
